blocks.heading: Why Claude Adoption Stalls After the First Prompt
blocks.description: Access alone does not create shared habits, safe-use boundaries or repeatable workflows. Without a practical adoption plan, people remain stuck with isolated experiments and inconsistent results.

steps.heading: People stay stuck in basic chat
steps.description: Most users ask one-off questions and stop there. They miss the value of Cowork, Projects, skills and other ways Claude can support recurring work.

steps.heading: The wrong Claude tool gets used
steps.description: Chat, Cowork and Code are designed for different jobs. Without a simple mental model, people choose the wrong mode, overcomplicate the task or avoid it altogether.

steps.heading: Every team invents its own way
steps.description: Useful context, constraints and skills live inside one person’s chat history. The next person starts from scratch, so quality varies wildly and the organisation accumulates dozens of competing approaches instead of one standard.

steps.heading: Quick call to map goals
steps.description:
We map your objectives, attendee experience, approved tools, data-handling requirements and the workflows your team most wants to improve. We then tailor the Foundation session to your industry and use cases, and prepare relevant scenarios.

We design the curriculum close to the delivery date on purpose. AI is moving fast, so what we teach reflects what Claude can do the week you are in the room, not what it could do last quarter.

steps.heading: Foundation training and pilot
steps.description:
Your pilot group completes a practical half-day at your office with two SSW presenters: one leading the teaching, one mentoring attendees through the hands-on exercises so nobody gets left behind.

The group then applies Claude to real work and runs internal sessions. This reveals which habits stick and where the real bottlenecks are.

steps.heading: Check-in and Advanced build
steps.description: We review the pilot results and plan the Advanced session. Two SSW presenters then work with your experienced users to build skills, prototype solutions and define practical implementation options.

blocks.heading: A two-tier program built for **Claude adoption**
blocks.body: The Foundation session gives your pilot group the habits and confidence to use Claude effectively. After the team applies the learning to real work, the Advanced session turns the most valuable opportunities into skills, prototypes and a practical implementation plan.

accordionItems.label: Foundation - What Claude Is and Where It Fits
accordionItems.content:
Understand what Claude is good at, where it is limited and where human judgement is still required.

Your team learns the principles for using Claude safely, responsibly and effectively in day-to-day business work.

accordionItems.label: Foundation - A Shared Way of Working with AI
accordionItems.content:
Agree what “good” looks like for your organisation: what work is worth handing to Claude, where the safe-use boundaries sit, and what shared language your teams use to talk about AI work.

Your pilot group leaves with a common standard they can take back and spread through their own teams.

accordionItems.label: Foundation - Chat, Cowork and Code
accordionItems.content:
Learn when the conversation itself is the work, when to hand Claude a task and when Claude Code is the right tool for a software team.

Participants leave with a clear mental model for choosing the appropriate Claude mode for each job.

accordionItems.label: Foundation - Prompting and Everyday Work
accordionItems.content:
Practise giving Claude clear goals, context, constraints and examples.

Your team applies these techniques to relevant finance, operations and everyday business tasks rather than working through generic demonstrations.

accordionItems.label: Foundation - Applied Workflow Scenarios
accordionItems.content:
Work through practical scenarios based on relevant real-world workflows. Learn how to package these into reusable and sharable skills.

The session finishes with questions, useful tips and clear next steps for what the pilot group should test and share internally.

accordionItems.label: Advanced - Using Claude Code
accordionItems.content: Starting using Claude Code and vibing up solutions - get comfortable with the processes and best practice in getting the results you want.

accordionItems.label: Advanced - Skills, Prototypes and Automation
accordionItems.content:
Two SSW presenters work with your experienced users to design custom Claude skills, specify valuable use cases and rapidly prototype working solutions.

The session can also explore automation and integration patterns, deployment options, solution architecture and the business case for further investment.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.answer:
Foundation Training is $5,200 + GST.

Advanced Training is $5,200 + GST.

The total for both tiers is $10,400 + GST, but either could be done separately if needed.

Each fee includes a half-day onsite session, dedicated preparation and two SSW presenters: one leading the teaching and one mentoring attendees through the hands-on work. Any additional consulting, development or implementation work can be scoped separately.

faqs.question: Do attendees need to know how to code?
faqs.answer:
No coding experience is required. These sessions are designed for a mixed business audience and is suitable for finance, operations, leadership and technical team members. Claude Code is introduced so the group understands where it fits, but Foundation Training is not a software development course.

The advanced course introduces Vibe Coding, but this is doable by anyone.

faqs.question: How long is the training?
faqs.answer:
Each training tier is delivered as a separate half-day onsite session.

Advanced Training is another half-day session, scheduled after the pilot group has applied the Foundation learning and completed a planning check-in with SSW.

faqs.question: Who should attend?
faqs.answer:
Foundation Training is for pilot groups and people who are new to Claude or are still developing consistent working habits.

It is suitable for business, finance, operations and relevant technical team members.

Advanced Training is for experienced users who have already applied Claude to real work and can bring specific bottlenecks, workflows or solution ideas into the room.

The appropriate group size is confirmed during planning so participants receive useful support during the hands-on exercises.

faqs.question: Will this give us a consistent approach across the company?
faqs.answer:
That is the intent. Foundation Training gives everyone the same mental model for Chat, Cowork and Code, and the same safe-use boundaries.

Advanced Training turns the best of what your people discover into custom Claude skills, so a good workflow becomes company property rather than one person’s chat history.

The pilot group is chosen so they can carry that standard back into their own teams.

faqs.question: What will our team take away?
faqs.answer:
After Foundation Training, your team will have a shared understanding of Chat, Cowork and Code, practical prompting techniques, safe-use principles and a focused list of workflows to test.

After Advanced Training, your team may leave with custom Claude skills, working prototypes, documented use cases and clearer options for automation, integration, architecture and further implementation.
